renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: family_msa
  title: Family alignment
  description: |-
    Each row is a sequence of a protein family, aligned to the family representative on top, and each column is an alignment position coloured by residue type. It answers how well the members of a family line up and where they differ.
    How to read: columns of one colour are conserved positions, and a block of gaps marks an insertion or a member that does not cover that region. Sequences with a low identity to the representative are the divergent members, which may be fragments or distant relatives. Brush columns to follow the residues on the structure and the sequence track.
    Lines and annotations: this module takes the first row of each alignment file as the family representative and measures each row's identity against it. The consensus row and the conservation bars are computed from the displayed rows, which this module caps at 500 per family in file order, not a FAMSA setting.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27670777/
  kind: msa
  roles:
    msa_id: msa_id
    seq_id: seq_id
    sequence: aligned_sequence
    rank: rank
    identity: identity

- component: card
  id: aligned_rows
  title: Aligned sequences
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of aligned rows across the families in view, and the strip gives how many distinct sequences they are. It answers how large the alignments are.
    How to read: a distinct count below the row count means the same sequence sits in more than one family. Rows are capped at 500 per family, so a very large family is not shown in full.
  column: seq_id
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: aligned rows, with the distinct sequences

- component: card
  id: aligned_identity
  title: Identity to the representative
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median identity between an aligned sequence and its family representative, and the box shows the spread. It answers how tight the families are.
    How to read: a high median means close relatives in a coherent family. A low median with a long lower tail holds distant or fragmentary members, which are worth checking before building a model from the family.
    Note: identity is measured over the columns both sequences share, so a short fragment can read as highly identical.
  column: identity
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread
  headline: true

- component: table
  title: Alignment table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sequence of a family alignment, with its family, its rank, the aligned sequence, its identity to the representative and the share of the representative it covers. It answers the exact members behind the alignment tile.
    How to read: sort by identity or coverage to find the members that fit the family least.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: conservation_track
  title: Conservation along the sequence
  description: |-
    Each position is a residue of the family representative, with a lane for its conservation score and a lane for its conservation class. It answers which stretches of the protein are conserved across the family and which vary.
    How to read: runs of high scores mark constrained regions, often a fold core or an active site, and low runs mark loops or variable linkers. Brush a stretch to light up the same residues on the structure and the alignment.
    Lines and annotations: the score is one minus the normalised Shannon entropy of the alignment column, discounted by the share of gaps, so 1 is an invariant gap-free column. The classes are cut at 0.7 and 0.4 by this catalog's recipe; they are not published cut-offs.
  kind: sequence_track
  config:
    value_label: Conservation score
  roles:
    position: position
    entity: entity
    residue: residue
    value: value
    category: category

- component: advanced_viz
  id: conservation_structure
  title: Conservation on the structure
  description: |-
    The 3D structure of the family representative, folded on demand from its sequence and coloured by the residue conservation score. It answers where the conserved residues sit in space.
    How to read: a conserved patch on the surface suggests a binding or catalytic site, while conserved residues buried in the core usually hold the fold. Variable residues on the surface are typical of regions free to change.
    Lines and annotations: the colour is the conservation score, the same one drawn along the sequence, from 0 for a diverse column to 1 for an invariant one.
    Note: the structure is a prediction made from the sequence, not an experimental one.
  kind: molecule_3d
  config:
    color_mode: value
  roles:
    position: position
    entity: entity
    value: value
    category: category
    sequence: sequence

- component: advanced_viz
  id: conservation_profile
  title: Conservation profile
  description: |-
    Each curve is a protein family: the conservation score at every residue position of its representative. It answers how conserved a family is along its length and how families compare.
    How to read: a curve that stays high is a tightly conserved family, and one that stays low is a diverse one. Peaks and valleys locate the conserved and variable regions.
    Lines and annotations: the score is one minus the normalised Shannon entropy of the alignment column, discounted by the share of gaps. Positions follow the numbering of the representative, without gaps.
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: Residue position
    y_title: Conservation score
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    series: entity
    x: position
    y: value

- component: card
  id: residue_conservation
  title: Residue conservation
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median conservation score over every residue of the families in view, and the box shows the spread. It answers how conserved the families are overall.
    How to read: a high median means a tight family. A box reaching to low values holds many variable residues, which is normal for a divergent family.
  column: value
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: figure
  title: Distribution of conservation scores
  description: |-
    Each bar counts residues in a conservation score bin, split by conservation class. It answers how many residues are conserved, intermediate or variable.
    How to read: a pile at high scores is a conserved family, and a pile at low scores is a divergent one. A two-humped shape means a conserved core and variable loops.
    Lines and annotations: the classes are cut at 0.7 and 0.4 by this catalog's recipe, a fixed binning of the score and not a published threshold.
     The dashed line is the median conservation score of this table, a reference
    computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of FAMSA.
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: value
    color: category
    labels:
      value: Conservation score
      category: Conservation class
  reference_lines:
  - axis: x
    stat: median
    column: value

- component: table
  title: Residue table
  description: |-
    Each row is a residue of a family representative, with its position, conservation score and class, the most frequent residue of its column, how many members have a residue there and the number of members. It answers the exact values behind the conservation tiles.
    How to read: filter by family and sort by score to list its most conserved residues.
